# Tunables

Every engine threshold, from the KDoc in `engine/src/commonMain/kotlin/pianoanchor/engine/Tunables.kt`.

| Name | Value | Meaning | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CHORD_CLUSTER_MS` | 90 | Notes whose onsets fall within this many milliseconds of a cluster's first note form one chord. | a chord is one physical gesture, so the window is absolute (not tempo-scaled, not widened for beginners). | practice-mode scorers group chord tones within 50–90 ms; score-alignment research uses a tighter 35 ms simultaneity threshold (Nakamura et al., ISMIR 2017). 90 ms suits beginners. |
| `SYSEX_MAX_BYTES` | 65_536 | Largest System Exclusive payload (bytes between 0xF0 and 0xF7) the MIDI parser keeps; longer ones are discarded. | bounds memory if a device never sends 0xF7. | MIDI 1.0 sets no SysEx length limit; 64 KiB is far above any message the app reads (identity replies and parameter reads are tens of bytes). |
| `BLE_SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS` | 12_000 | How long a Bluetooth LE MIDI scan runs, in milliseconds, before it stops by itself. | a piano that is on and free advertises often, so a short scan finds it; stopping early saves battery. | a surveyed open-source BLE MIDI app scans for 12 s; revisit after the T8 soak test. |
| `BLE_RECONNECT_INITIAL_MS` | 1_000 | Wait before the first attempt to reopen a dropped Bluetooth LE MIDI device, in milliseconds; each further attempt waits twice as long, up to [BLE_RECONNECT_MAX_MS]. | a brief radio drop should recover quickly, without retrying in a tight loop. | initial guess; revisit after the T8 60-minute soak test. |
| `BLE_RECONNECT_MAX_MS` | 30_000 | Longest wait between attempts to reopen a dropped Bluetooth LE MIDI device, in milliseconds. | caps the backoff so a piano that comes back is found soon, without hammering the Bluetooth stack. | initial guess; revisit after the T8 soak test. |
| `BLE_RECONNECT_GIVE_UP_MS` | 300_000 | Total backoff waiting, in milliseconds, after which the adapter stops trying to reopen a dropped Bluetooth LE MIDI device: no attempt starts once the waits since the drop would add up to more than this (the time the attempts themselves take is not counted). | covers briefly walking away from the piano, then stops draining the battery. | initial guess; revisit after the T8 soak test. |
| `MONITOR_RECONNECT_GIVE_UP_MS` | 2 * BLE_RECONNECT_GIVE_UP_MS | How long, in milliseconds after the selected device drops, the note monitor waits for it to be open again before it stops reconnecting and reports the device as unavailable. | the monitor cannot see when the adapter stops retrying. The adapter's [BLE_RECONNECT_GIVE_UP_MS] counts only its waits, not its attempts (about 13 with this backoff, each up to [BLE_LISTED_TIMEOUT_MS] plus Android's open time), so the monitor waits twice as long. Giving up late only shows "Reconnecting…" longer; giving up early would hide a piano that came back. A USB piano unplugged that long is reported too, instead of waiting forever. | derived from [BLE_RECONNECT_GIVE_UP_MS]; revisit once the T8 soak test measures how long attempts take. |
| `BLE_LISTED_TIMEOUT_MS` | 5_000 | How long, in milliseconds, a Bluetooth LE MIDI device that Android reports as opened may take to show up in the device list; if it doesn't, the open counts as failed and the handle is closed. | Android lists the device before it hands back the opened device, so this only bounds the rare case of a link that drops in between; without it `connect` could wait forever. | initial guess, far above the expected delay of one main-looper callback; revisit after the T8 test. |
| `MONITOR_LOG_LINES` | 50 | How many lines the note monitor keeps in its live log (newest first); older lines are dropped. | enough to read back the last phrase played, while bounding the work of redrawing the log. | UI choice agreed in the note-monitor grill (2026-11-11). |
| `MONITOR_RECORDING_MAX_MS` | 1_800_000 | Longest note-monitor recording, in milliseconds after its first event; recording stops there with a notice. | bounds memory (a few MB of messages at most) while a fixture session lasts minutes. | agreed in the note-monitor grill (2026-11-11). |
| `IDENTITY_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS` | 1_000 | How long, in milliseconds after sending the MIDI Identity Request, the app waits for the Identity Reply before it stores the piano without an identity. | a piano that answers does so within tens of milliseconds, and a short wait keeps connecting snappy; many Bluetooth pianos never answer, so the wait is paid often. | MIDI 1.0 sets no deadline; initial guess (slice 1.5 spec), revisit after the hardware check. |
| `BAND_CLEAN_MIN_ACCURACY` | 0.95 | Lowest accuracy (0.0–1.0) of a wait-mode attempt graded `Band.CLEAN`. | "clean" should allow at most a rare slip on longer passages. | matches the M1 ≥ 95% classification bar; initial guess, tune from the learner's data. |
| `BAND_GOOD_MIN_ACCURACY` | 0.80 | Lowest accuracy (0.0–1.0) of a wait-mode attempt graded `Band.GOOD`; below it the band is `KEEP_PRACTISING`. | about one slip per five notes is still a run worth building on. | initial guess (slice 1.7 spec); tune from the learner's data. |
| `KEY_FLASH_MS` | 260 | How long, in milliseconds, the practice screen's key strip flashes a pressed key as correct or wrong. | long enough to see which key was hit, short enough not to linger into the next note. | the Living Studio mock (slice 1.9 spec). |
| `TIMING_TOLERANCE_MS` | 60 | Floor of the early/late band, in milliseconds: an onset further than max(this, [TIMING_TOLERANCE_BEAT_FRACTION] of a beat) from where the tempo puts it is `EARLY` or `LATE`. | at fast tempos a fraction of a beat gets too tight for a beginner's hands; 60 ms stays lenient. | starting value, owner-agreed in the M1 grill; calibrated in M7. |
| `TIMING_TOLERANCE_BEAT_FRACTION` | 0.125 | The early/late band as a fraction of a beat (a quarter note); the band is max([TIMING_TOLERANCE_MS], this). | at slow tempos the band grows with the beat; an eighth of a beat is clearly off, less is expressive. | starting value, owner-agreed in the M1 grill; calibrated in M7. |
| `HESITATION_GAP_RATIO` | 2.0 | A step whose gap from the previous step is at least this many times the expected gap (and at least [HESITATION_MIN_MS]) is a `HESITATION`, not a late note. | a gap twice the expected one reads as a stop, not as a rushed or dragged note. | starting value, owner-agreed in the M1 grill; calibrated in M7. |
| `HESITATION_MIN_MS` | 400 | Shortest gap before a step, in milliseconds, that can be a `HESITATION` (with [HESITATION_GAP_RATIO]). | at fast tempos a doubled gap is still short, and short gaps aren't stops. | starting value, owner-agreed in the M1 grill; calibrated in M7. |
| `MISTOUCH_WINDOW_MS` | 40 | A softer key one or two semitones from a louder correct note, starting within this many milliseconds of it, is a `MISTOUCH` (a brushed key), not an extra note. | a brushed neighbour key sounds almost together with the intended one. | starting value, owner-agreed in the M1 grill; calibrated in M7. |
| `NOTE_SHORT_RATIO` | 0.5 | A note sounding for less than this fraction of its written length is `TOO_SHORT`. | under half the written length is clearly clipped, not a phrasing choice. | starting value, owner-agreed in the M1 grill; calibrated in M7. |
| `NOTE_LONG_RATIO` | 1.5 | A note sounding for more than this fraction of its written length is `TOO_LONG`. | over half again the written length is clearly held too long. | starting value, owner-agreed in the M1 grill; calibrated in M7. |
